correctness.rationale: An exact digit recurrence yields B(F)Y=A(F)r. Because D(0)=1, D(F) has no nonzero formal-series kernel with constant term zero, so E(F)Y=C(F)r. For Bezout HC+JE=1, W=H(F)Y+J(F)r satisfies E(F)W=r. The simple pole of r at x=1 forces ramification divisible by 2^deg(E), equalling the degree upper bound, proving irreducibility. All zero masks and nonleast periods are covered. Finite independent coefficient and automaton checks confirm formulas but are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 papers give masked digit sums, their automata and sequence transformations; a 2025 paper provides general algebraic-series complexity bounds. Neither inspected exact statement nor OEIS records the gcd-indexed exact minimal algebraic degree for all periodic masks, nor the degree-four minimal polynomial of the new meta-automatic example. The mathematical statement and stronger coverage, not titles alone, were compared; published-priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: Equivalent gcd/ramification classification may be implicit in unindexed literature on additive polynomials or periodic digit sums.
Not every page of each broader source was inspected; in particular no comprehensive historical priority proof is claimed.

value.rationale: The exact minimal algebraic degree of a coefficient series is a natural and nonautomatic invariant. This result classifies every periodic binary position mask by a computable polynomial gcd, including a complete 3-period family exhibiting all four degree values 1,2,4,8. It explains the specific quartic degree of the recently introduced M2 and distinguishes algebraicity from minimality; not a small table recomputation or a trivial corollary of automaticity.
